title: Ideal-power quotient of a coherent formal-module limit sheaf
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme, $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, $G$ a coherent $J$-adic formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and $n\in\mathbb N$. Write $L=\varprojlim G$ for its limit in $\mathcal O_Y$-module sheaves. There is an isomorphism $e:L/J^{n+1}L\simeq G_n$ such that the quotient projection followed by $e$ equals the canonical limit projection $L\to G_n$. The indexing convention labels level $n+1$ by $n$.

source.place: Lemma 087W, formula M/I^n M=M_n; local uniqueness in first half of Lemma 088B. Sources read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087W and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088B.

proof.text: Evaluation on each affine open V preserves limits. The unique isomorphism of limiting cones carries the evaluated canonical projection to the canonical projection of the evaluated tower. Apply the affine projection theorem to obtain surjectivity and the kernel formula J(V)^(n+1) times the entire section limit.

Apply the ideal-power clauses of ideal_times_quasiCoherent_affine_sections to the quasi-coherent unit sheaf: on each affine V the range of the power inclusion is J(V)^(n+1). Multiplication followed by the limit projection vanishes on pure tensor germs, since the ideal power annihilates the level. Pure tensors generate tensor stalks, so the composite sheaf morphism is zero and its sheaf image lies in the kernel. Conversely every affine kernel section is a finite sum of ideal-power scalars times limit sections by the affine kernel formula. Lift its scalars through the power inclusion and form pure tensor sections, yielding a preimage under multiplication. The kernel therefore lies in the image locally, and the two subsheaves coincide. This argument neither assumes quasi-coherence of the limit nor assumes that evaluation preserves arbitrary sheaf images.

Affine surjectivity makes the projection an epimorphism of sheaves. The kernel-image identification makes it a cokernel of the multiplication-image inclusion in this abelian category. Uniqueness of cokernels gives the isomorphism from the formalModuleQuotient cokernel, with its required projection equation. Empty opens, zero sheaves, J=0 and J=1 obey the same argument.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_limit_quotient {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (G : CoherentFormalModule Y J) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : formalModuleQuotient J (n + 1) (limit G.obj) ≅ G.obj.obj (op n),
      formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) (limit G.obj) ≫ e.hom =
        limit.π G.obj (op n)
